keywords: HistoryPanel 怎么用 plotly 画图
title: Plot a HistoryPanel with hp.plot()
summary: hp.plot() is the single chart entry. Candles need a full OHLC family already on the panel. interactive=True uses Plotly; plot does not invent indicator columns.
narrative:
The recommended chart entry is HistoryPanel.plot(). Chart type follows the htypes already on the panel: a full OHLC family can render as candles; otherwise you typically get lines. plot does not invent indicator columns—build MACD, SMA, or other series first (research_preset or kline on the analysis card), then plot.

interactive=False (default) uses matplotlib for static figures. interactive=True uses Plotly for zoom and hover. In Jupyter, FigureWidget is preferred when anywidget and ipywidgets are available; otherwise an HTML wrapper may appear.

layout chooses overlay, stack, or auto for multiple shares. shares subsets the symbols. highlight can mark max/min or a condition mask. plotly_backend_app selects auto, FigureWidget, or html when interactive is on. Many shares may be capped with a warning to avoid overcrowding.

Asking how to draw a K-line at explain level means: put open/high/low/close on the panel, then call hp.plot(). This card does not teach panel creation or factor math, and it does not walk advanced 2.6–2.8 demo loops.
python_code:
import qteasy as qt
hp = qt.get_kline(htypes='open, high, low, close, vol', shares='000300.SH', rows=120, as_panel=True)
fig = hp.plot()
# fig2 = hp.plot(interactive=True)  # Plotly when installed
risk_notes: Incomplete OHLC will not produce a candle chart. Adj OHLC families such as open|b..close|b must be complete as a set for candles.
